This article describes the internal architecture of GiottoVisuals for
contributors. It covers how plot functions get their data out of a `giotto`
object, how that data reaches a geom, and the reasoning behind decisions that
are not obvious from the code.

## Package Layers

A plot function moves through four layers, top to bottom:

| Layer | Where | Responsibility |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| Entry | `vis_spatial_gg.R`, `vis_spatial_in_situ.R`, `vis_spatial_plotly.R`, `plot_*.R` | User-facing function, argument defaults, orchestration |
| Data input | `GiottoClass` getters, `spatValues()`, `combine*Data()`, `.gg_materialize()` | Pull values out of the gobject into a `data.table` |
| Render | `gg_info_layers.R`, `gg_param.R`, `aux_defaults.R`, `color_palettes.R` | Turn a table plus params into ggplot layers |
| Output | `aux_output.R`, `aux_save.R` | Show / save / return, per `giottoInstructions` |

The data input and render layers are not separated by a function boundary.
Entry functions interleave the two in a single body — `.spatPlot2D_single()`
fetches locations, network, grid and metadata, subsets them, and constructs
geoms in the same ~460-line closure. Recognizing this seam is the precondition
for most of the work in [Planned Work](#planned-work).

## Data Input

### The four input paths

There is no single data-input API. Four paths coexist, in rough order of
preference for new code:

1. **`spatValues()`** — the funnel. Give it `feats` and it searches the gobject
   for them. Preferred for anything that is "a named column of values per
   cell".
2. **`combine*Data()` / `combineMetadata()`** — joined tables when a plot needs
   coordinates, metadata, polygons or overlapped points together. Used by
   `spatInSituPlotPoints()` and the `spat*Plot` family.
3. **Direct slot getters** — `getSpatialLocations()`, `getSpatialNetwork()`,
   `getDimReduction()`, `getSpatialGrid()`, `getGiottoImage()`,
   `getExpression()`. Used where the thing wanted is a whole slot, not a set of
   named values: networks, grids, images, embeddings. A network's getter is not
   enough on its own: it returns edges, and the endpoint coordinates needed to
   draw them are attached with `GiottoClass::annotateSpatialNetwork()`. The seam
   and what follows from it — live coordinates, an inner join, and nodes coming
   from the locations rather than the edges — are in GiottoClass's design
   article under Networks, and in ADR 0004.
4. **`.gg_materialize()`** — not a fetch. A pre-narrow applied before any of the
   above (see [View / space pre-narrow](#view-space-pre-narrow)).

All of them return eagerly. `spatValues()` and the `combine*` functions return
`data.table`; the getters are called with `output = "data.table"` /
`"networkDT"` / `"matrix"`.

### `spatValues()` as the funnel

`spatValues(gobject, feats, ...)` is a plain function in GiottoClass, not a
generic. It walks a fixed search order and returns the first slot that holds
every requested feature, as a `data.table` keyed on `cell_ID`:

```
cell expression -> cell metadata -> spatial locations
  -> spatial enrichment -> dim reduction -> polygon info
```

Passing a location parameter (`expression_values`, `spat_enr_name`,
`dim_reduction_name`, ...) scopes the search to that one slot, which also
relaxes the all-or-nothing match into a partial match with a message.

The consequence for plot functions is that `cell_color = "leiden_clus"`,
`cell_color = "Gfap"` and `cell_color = "sdimx"` are all one call with no
branch at the call site. Feature-value collection in `spatFeatPlot2D_single()`,
`dimFeatPlot2D()`, the 3D variants, `violinPlot()`, `dotPlot()` and
`plotRidge()` all route this way.

### View / space pre-narrow {#view-space-pre-narrow}

Plot functions that accept `view` / `space` call `.gg_materialize()` as their
first statement, before any defaults are resolved or data is fetched.

```r
gobject <- .gg_materialize(gobject, view, space,
    slots = c("cell_metadata", "expression", "spatial_enrichment"))
```

`slots` names the slots that plot reads, from the canonical set in
`GiottoClass::materialize()`. The resolver runs **once** for the listed slots,
so the predicate or crop is evaluated a single time no matter how many
`combine*` / getter calls the plot body then makes.

`.gg_materialize()` exists as a helper rather than an inline call because
`view = NULL` has to be the default, so that callers without a view see normal
behavior, and every call site would otherwise carry its own
`if (!is.null(view) || !is.null(space))` guard. The helper folds that guard into
one place — do not inline it back. The guard is an early return, not a dispatch
workaround: `materialize()` has `view = "NULL"` methods for both `giotto` and
`giottoMulti`, and the guard only keeps a plot with neither knob set from paying
for a resolver pass that narrows nothing.

What `materialize()` has no method for is a **recipe object** — it dispatches on
`signature(giotto, character)` and `(giotto, "NULL")`, never on `giottoView`.
That is the contract, not an omission: a view or space is passed by name so that
a result can say which one produced it. `.gg_materialize()` asserts it with
`checkmate::assert_string()` rather than letting it surface as "unable to find an
inherited method".

It is backend-agnostic by construction: `materialize()` selects
`dataTableCoordinator` for in-memory gobjects and `parquetCoordinator` for
`gsource`-backed ones via `.default_view_coordinator()`. Nothing in
GiottoVisuals chooses.

#### The in-situ window is also a view

`spatInSituPlotPoints()`'s `xlim` / `ylim` are not a separate mechanism.
`.sissp_window_view()` records the window as a crop step on a scratch view of a
local copy of the gobject, rather than cropping the polygon carrier eagerly —
a carrier crop works on a `SpatVector` and has no route on a disk-backed store,
whereas a crop step resolves through whichever coordinator the object
registers. It uses `geom = "poly"` so a polygon overlapping the window survives
even when its centroid does not, matching what the eager crop did.

`.sissp_window_view()` also accepts a `view =`, which copies a caller-supplied
view onto the scratch name first so the window lands last. Nothing passes it
today: `spatInSituPlotPoints()` resolves the caller's view eagerly through
`.gg_materialize()` at the top of the body, so by the time the window is
recorded there is no view left to compose with and it becomes a second one.
Two resolver passes on the polygon path, where the rest of this section
promises one — harmless, but the composed form would need `view` threaded
through `.sissp_polygon()`, `.sissp_points()` and `.sissp_image()` instead of
materializing once up front. Which ordering is right when a window and a view
are given together is still open.

### There is no backed-vs-unbacked branch here, by design {#no-backed-branch}

A disk-backed gobject is still class `giotto`. Backing lives one level down, in
the subobjects — a `parquetExprStore` inside the `exprObj`, a `parquetStore`
inside the `spatLocsObj`, a `parquetEdgeStore` in `@network`. S4 dispatch on
`gobject` therefore cannot separate backed from unbacked, and a plot function
that tried to branch on it would be branching on the wrong thing.

Backed data works today because the getters narrow before they materialize.
`spatValues()`'s expression branch subsets to the requested features first and
only then coerces:

```r
e[][present, , drop = FALSE] |> t_flex() |> as("dgCMatrix") |> as.matrix()
```

For a handful of features that is cheap on any carrier. It is, however,
hardcoded to the sparse in-memory route, and there is no seam at which a store
could serve those columns natively.

**Rule for this package:** no `inherits(x, "dataStore")` checks in
GiottoVisuals. GiottoVisuals imports only GiottoUtils and GiottoClass and must
stay that way. Any behavior that has to differ by carrier is expressed as a
generic in GiottoClass with an in-memory default method, and implemented for
stores in GiottoDisk. `.gg_materialize()` is the model: one call, no branch,
the right coordinator chosen below.

## Render

### Layer functions

`gg_info_layers.R` holds the render primitives. Each takes a ggplot object plus
a prepared table and returns the object with one layer added:

| Function | Adds |
|----------|------|
| `plot_spat_point_layer_ggplot()` | Cell points, fill-capable |
| `plot_spat_point_layer_ggplot_noFILL()` | Cell points, color-only |
| `plot_spat_voronoi_layer_ggplot()` | Voronoi tessellation |
| `plot_cell_polygon_layer()` | Cell polygons |
| `plot_feature_points_layer()` | Transcript / feature points |
| `plot_feature_raster_density_layer()`, `plot_feature_hexbin_layer()` | Binned feature density |
| `plot_spat_image_layer_ggplot()` | Background image |
| `plot_spat_scatterpie_layer_ggplot()` | Deconvolution pies |
| `plot_network_layer_ggplot()` | Network edges |
| `plot_point_layer_ggplot()`, `..._noFILL()` | Dimension-reduction points |

These take prepared tables, never a gobject — with the exception of
`plot_spat_image_layer_ggplot()`, which needs the gobject to resolve the image
and its extent. The `.sissp_*()` helpers in `vis_spatial_in_situ.R` sit one
level above and do take a gobject: fetch, then delegate to a layer function.
They are the closest thing in the package to an explicit collect/render split
and are the pattern to follow.

### Color resolution order {#color-order}

`cell_color` (and the `polygon_fill` / `feat_color` equivalents) is
deliberately overloaded. The resolution order below is canonical and is applied
by every point and polygon layer function:

1. `NULL` — default to `"lightblue"`, no mapping.
2. Character or numeric vector of `length > 1`:
   - numeric or factor — treated as per-cell values, attached as `temp_color`
     and mapped. Errors if the length does not match the row count.
   - character — must be all valid color codes, applied as a literal fill.
3. Character of `length 1`:
   - not a column name in the data — must be a valid color code, applied as a
     literal fill. Errors otherwise.
   - a column name:
     - numeric or integer column and `color_as_factor = FALSE` — continuous
       gradient, honoring `gradient_limits` and `gradient_midpoint`.
     - otherwise — coerced to factor, discrete scale.

The five layer functions that implement this each carry a one-line pointer back
to this section instead of restating the ladder.

### Palette defaults

Color defaults resolve through three levels, closest wins:

```
function argument  ->  giottoInstructions  ->  global option
```

`set_default_color_discrete()` / `set_default_color_continuous()` and their
`_cell` / `_poly` / `_feat` / `_heatmap` wrappers implement this. The global
options are initialized in `zzz.R`:

| Option | Default | Scope |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `giotto.color_d_pal` | `"distinct"` | Discrete palette |
| `giotto.color_d_rev` | `FALSE` | Discrete reversal |
| `giotto.color_d_strategy` | `"interpolate"` | Discrete expansion strategy |
| `giotto.color_cd_pal` | `c("blue", "white", "red")` | Continuous divergent |
| `giotto.color_cs_pal` | `"viridis"` | Continuous sequential |
| `giotto.color_c_rev` | `FALSE` | Continuous reversal |

A palette resolves to a **factory function** (`n` in, colors out), not a vector,
so that the number of levels does not need to be known at default-resolution
time. `set_default_color_*()` returns early when given a function, wraps a
multi-entry character vector with `simple_palette_factory()`, and treats a
single string as a `getColors()` palette name.

These functions must keep inline fallback defaults for their `getOption()`
reads rather than relying on `zzz.R` having run: GiottoVisuals is frequently
loaded as a dependency or reached via `::` without being attached, in which case
`.onLoad`'s `init_option()` calls have not necessarily populated the options.

### Params and aesthetics

`gg_param()` sorts a flat set of named arguments into a ggplot2 `aes` mapping
versus top-level geom parameters, by class: anything that is a `quosure`, a
`name`, or a language object becomes an aesthetic, everything else becomes a
top-level parameter. This lets layer functions accumulate params
unconditionally and sort once at the end.

`aes_string2()` exists because `ggplot2::aes_string()` was removed in ggplot2
v4. It also handles column names that parse as numeric literals (`"1"`, `"2"`),
which appear routinely as spatial-enrichment and cluster column names.

### Point rasterization budget

`giotto_point()` dispatches between `ggplot2::geom_point()`,
`scattermore::geom_scattermore()` and `scattermore::geom_scattermost()` on
`plot_method`, and computes the raster pixel dimensions from
`getOption("giotto.plot_point_raster", 5e5)` and the plot extent.

This is a **pixel** budget, not a row budget. It reduces the resolution the
points are rasterized into; it does not reduce the number of rows fetched, and
it only applies once the caller has already selected a scattermore method.
There is currently no row-count guard anywhere in the data path — see
[Planned Work](#planned-work).

Image resolution has a separate budget: `auto_image_resample()` uses
`giotto.plot_img_max_sample` (default `5e5`) and `terra::window()` to avoid
materializing large crops.

## Output Handling

Every plot function returns through `plot_output_handler()`, which reads
`show_plot` / `save_plot` / `return_plot` from the passed value when non-`NULL`
and otherwise from the object's `giottoInstructions`. Saving is delegated to
`all_plots_save_function()`.

## Multi-sample (`giottoMulti`)

`giottoMulti` is a sibling of `giotto` — both extend `gAny`, neither inherits
from the other. Plot functions handle it with two helpers rather than dispatch.

**`.gg_multi_dispatch_spatial()`** is the opt-in path. A spatial plot function
inserts a guard at the top of its body:

```r
spatPlot2D <- function(gobject, ..., view = NULL, space = NULL,
                       samples = NULL) {
    if (inherits(gobject, "giottoMulti")) {
        return(.gg_multi_dispatch_spatial(
            plot_fn = spatPlot2D,
            named = mget(setdiff(names(formals()), "...")),
            dots = list(...),    # omit if the fn has no `...`
            gobject = gobject, view = view, space = space,
            samples = samples
        ))
    }
    .gg_assert_giotto_single(gobject)
    ...
}
```

The helper pulls each requested child out of `gobject@objects` and re-calls
`plot_fn` on it as a single `giotto`, so the getters inside need no knowledge of
samples. Panels are combined with `cowplot::plot_grid()`, reusing the plot
function's existing `cow_n_col` / `cow_rel_h` / `cow_rel_w` / `cow_align`
arguments. Titles compose as user prefix plus sample name, but only when the
plot function actually has a `title` formal — `spatFeatPlot2D()` and
`spatCellPlot2D()` title their sub-panels by feature name and expose no
top-level `title`.

**`view` and `space` are applied once on the multi, before the panel loop**, so
the resolver's surviving-cell cache fills a single time and each per-child
getter chain pulls only its own slice. `space` in particular *has* to be applied
there rather than forwarded to the per-panel call: `materialize()` hands each
child the recipe scoped to its own name (`space_obj[samp]`), and that is the
last point at which the sample identity needed to pick a per-sample step still
exists. A panel child is a plain `giotto` with no name to resolve against.

**`.gg_assert_giotto_single()`** is what remains of the earlier single-sample-only
contract. It replaces `checkmate::assert_class(gobject, "giotto")`, whose "Must
inherit from class 'giotto'" reads as though the user passed something that is
not a Giotto object at all rather than as a missed dispatch. No public plot
function can reach its `giottoMulti` branch any more — the spatial ones return
through the dispatcher above their guard, and the non-spatial and dim-reduction
ones dropped the guard once their getters became gmulti-aware. What is left is
an invariant on the single-sample internals (`.spatPlot2D_single`,
`.dimPlot2D_single`), so the message names a missed dispatch inside the package
rather than telling a user a feature is missing.

### Which samples a space implies {#space-panel-scope}

A `space` sets the panel set **only when its membership is closed**.

A `combinedSpace` lays its members out relative to one another in one
coordinate system. A sample outside that layout has no position in the frame, so
drawing it would put an untransformed panel beside transformed ones: the space
defines the panels, and a `samples =` that escapes its membership is an error.

A `perSampleSpace` is open by design — an unscoped step means "whatever sample
it meets" — so `names()` on it lists the samples the recipe happens to mention,
not the samples it covers. Deriving a panel set from that would silently drop
children the space applies to perfectly well, so it reframes every panel without
narrowing which are drawn.

This is deliberately narrower than the rule for artifact *generators*, which
refuse an explicit sample scope that escapes the space at all. A panel set is
not an artifact: nothing is persisted under a name that would later read as
covering more than it does, and the scope is visible in the call that produced
the figure. So the constraint is applied only where the frame itself makes an
outside sample meaningless.

## Design Decisions

### Plot functions are closures, not generics

There is no S4 dispatch on `gobject` anywhere in the package. The `setMethod()`
calls that exist are for `giottoSankeyPlan`, `show`, and
`gg_annotation_raster()` — which dispatches on the *image* class
(`giottoImage` / `giottoLargeImage` / `giottoAffineImage` / `list`) against a
`ggUnionClass` plot object, and is the one place dispatch earns its keep.

This is a consequence of [the backing rule](#no-backed-branch) rather than an
oversight: the axis a plot function would most want to dispatch on is not
visible in the `gobject` class.

### Entry functions take flat formals

`.spatPlot2D_single()` has roughly 60 formals. This is deliberate for the
user-facing surface — it keeps every knob discoverable through `?spatPlot2D`
and tab-completion, and it is what existing Giotto users expect. It is not
deliberate for the internals, where any wrapper that needs to re-dispatch a
plot call has to reconstruct it from `formals()`.

### `plot_output_handler()` is a single function

It reads settings, prints, saves and returns in one pass. Splitting it into a
read step producing a `giottoPlotOutput` and a do step consuming one has been
sketched but not adopted; the sketch survives as commented code in
`aux_output.R`. The motivation would be testability — as written, the decision
logic cannot be exercised without producing a plot.

## Planned Work {#planned-work}

In dependency order. None of this is committed; it is recorded so the reasoning
is not re-derived.

1. **Extract the collect phase into named internals.** Split each `*_single`
   into a `.plotdata_*()` and a `.render_*()`. Mechanical, no behavior change.
   `.sissp_polygon()` / `.sissp_points()` and the violin / ridge / dotplot
   bodies already have the shape; `.spatPlot2D_single()` and
   `spatFeatPlot2D_single()` are the ones that need it. Prerequisite for
   everything below.

2. **A render-budget generic.** Something like `plotPrepare(x, budget)` in
   GiottoClass, default method identity, with store methods in GiottoDisk that
   push the reduction down (stride sample, bbox crop, SQL-side hexbin
   aggregate). GiottoDisk already has this logic — `.arrow_sample_max_rows()`,
   the `giottodisk.plot_sample_max` option, the sedona stride sample — but it
   is sealed inside `setMethod("plot", "parquetGeomStore")` and reachable only
   by calling `plot()` on a bare store. Highest value per line changed, and the
   difference between a spatial plot of a large backed points store working and
   exhausting memory.

3. **A carrier output mode for collectors.** Return what the slot natively
   holds rather than forcing a `data.table`, and force only at the geom
   boundary. `spatValues()` needs an `output =` argument, and its expression
   branch needs to route through a generic so a backed store can serve a narrow
   feature set as a column pull instead of `dgCMatrix` to dense.

4. **Push `select_cells` / `select_cell_groups` down to the fetch.** These are
   predicates, but they are applied after the data is in hand, as `data.table`
   filters in plot bodies. Expressed instead as view steps they would be
   evaluated once, at the source, on the backed side. `xlim` / `ylim` already
   work this way in `spatInSituPlotPoints()` — see
   [the in-situ window](#view-space-pre-narrow) — so the pattern is
   established; these two are what is left.

5. **Consolidate the request spec.** `GiottoClass::svkey` is already a
   declarative, serializable "data to fetch" object with a `@get` closure that
   `spatValues()` honors. Growing it is preferable to inventing a new spec
   class, and it composes with the view recipe.

Tests that check backed and unbacked parity should assert the **class** the
collector returns, not only the values — otherwise a parity test passes having
quietly materialized the whole store.
